info.title: Virtual Card Payments
info.description:
## Overview

The Virtual Card Payments API enables client applications to create virtual card payments according to their payment instructions. One can also read the card CVV and change the card status.

Please consult the **API developer portal** for details regarding:
- New v2 capabilities and v1 compatibilty.
- Three virtual card payment flows, a.k.a. remitTypes.
- Purchase authorizations, controls, and authorization webhooks.
- Bulk card intake and associated webhooks.

**V1 vs. V2**

In v2, virtual cards are based upon a Virtual Account Number or VAN. A v2 VAN card supports the enhancements documented within this specification.

Cards created using the v1 API, meaning a cardID issued in v1, can be used with the v2 API. However,
- A few incompatibilites exist (some v1 fields are no longer available).
- New v2 capabilities are not supported with a v1 cardID.

These differences are documented within this specification and at the API developer portal.

**Push Provisioning**

If a virtual card will be provisioned to a digital wallet, the _cardholderName_ value cannot be empty. Otherwise, attempting to use the push provisioning encryption APIs will fail.

See the digital wallets API specification for details regarding encryption.

**Valid characters**

Unless stated otherwise, strings allow the following special characters, including the 'space' character:

**` - = \ ] [ ' ; / . , ! @ # $ % & * ( ) _ + { } | : " ? < >**

### Revision history

Last updated June 29, 2026. Expand _Revision history_ for details.

<details><summary>Revision history</summary>

- 2.7.0
  - Added POST, PATCH, DELETE _/payments/{paymentID}/invoices_ endpoints.
- 2.6.0
  - Added _PATCH /payments/{paymentID}_ endpoint.
  - Corrected _payment.invoices[].amount_ minimum to zero (not negative).
  - Corrected _GET /realtime-credit-details_ spec to match implementation.
- 2.5.0
  - Added /payments endpoints
  - Changes to virtualCard.amountRanges[]
    - Added authorizationAmountUsed field.
    - Corrected minimum and maximum data type from string to number.
- 2.4.0
  - Introduced digital wallet encryption endpoints for Apple and Google.
    See the Digital Wallet Push Provisioning 1.0.0 specification.
  - Added preAuthorizationAmount field to VAN virtual card schema.
    - Create and update requests and read response.
- 2.3.0
  - Introduced Account real time credit details API.
    See the Virtual Card Program Management 1.0.0 specification.
  - Introduced Instant Card API.
    See the Instant Card 1.0.0 specification.
- 2.2.0
  - Added Get-transactions and Search-transactions endpoints.
  - Added table of Merchant Category Codes.
  - Removed erroneous sequenceNumber from create request.
- 2.1.1
  - Removed 'discriminator remitType' as it causes code-generation to fail.
- 2.1.0
  - Introduced Bulk Card Intake API.
    See the Bulk Card 1.0.2 specification.
- 2.0.0
  - Added the following card attributes to Create-Card, Get-Card, and Update-Card
    - Cardholder name
    - Authorization status - suspend/unsuspend a card
    - Authorization controls
    - Daily effective times
    - MCC ranges
    - User attributes
  - Removed Get-CVV endpoint. CVV is available via Get-Card.
  - Removed accountUID from Get-Authorizations response.
  - Removed accountUID and accountID from Get-Card response.

</details>

post.description:
For the given organization and payment account, create a virtual card.

When creating a card, the client (payer) must indicate how the card details will be provided, or remitted to the supplier (payee), as designated by the remitType:

|remitType|Description|
|:--- |:--- |
|ClientRemit |The client will notify the payee separately|
|SupplierNotEnrolled |The system will notify the supplier via the details provided in the request|
|SupplierEnrolled |The system will notify the supplier via the Client-Supplier-Information (CSI) record, and optionally override recorded values with any provided in the request. **The payment account ID must be defined in CSI record.**|

If successful, a virtual card ID is returned. (This ID can be used interchangeably as an order ID in the Access Online Order API.)

These fields are only applicable if the payment account is part of virtual account number (VAN) program:
- userAttributes{}
- cardholderName
- authStatus
- preAuthorizationAmount
- authorizationControls{}
- dailyEffectiveTimes[]
- merchantCategoryCodeRanges[]

patch.description:
Update the specified card payment with the requested modifications. The request schema describes which fields can be updated and how to update them. This PATCH method adheres to the conventions of **JSON Merge Patch [RFC 7396](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)**, which defines a JSON payload syntax for adding, replacing, or removing one or more values. To summarize, only provide fields that need updating. - To change a value, populate the field with the desired value - To clear a value, use empty string "" or zero 0 - To leave a value unchanged, it must be absent from the request **NOTICE:** - Modifying will fail if the card status is canceled, closed, expired, or fulfilled. - Certain fields cannot be cleared or zeroed, as noted below in the request body schema. - The behavior of using **_null_** to update a value is undefined and may change in a future release.
_Do not use the null value with update until supported._ These fields are only applicable if the payment account is part of virtual account number (VAN) program: - userAttributes{} - cardholderName - authStatus - preAuthorizationAmount - authorizationControls{} - dailyEffectiveTimes[] - merchantCategoryCodeRanges[]

get.summary: Retrieve available credit balance detail for the virtual card.
get.description:
For the specified card, return the current available credit.

Credit details are updated nightly or when an authorization has occurred. Use this endpoint to retrieve the most recent credit details in real-time, prior to those events.

(One exception is immediately after the card is created, real-time credit details are not updated until one of those events occur.  For example, after creating a card and prior to the first nightly update, this endpoint returns the original credit details, not the most recent values. Thereafter, the most recent values are available.)

For account credit balance, see the [Available Credit](/products/virtual-card-payments/v2/available-credit-api-reference) API reference.

This request may fail during nightly maintenance, which begins at 7:30 PM Central Time and typically completes by 12:00 AM CT depending upon demand. During that time, the request will fail if the specified account is being processed. Retry the request after maintenance on the account has completed.

get.summary: Return authorizations for this card within a date range.
get.description:
Returns a list of authorizations within the date range, inclusive.

Up to 6 years of authorization history is retained, with a maximum search range of 180 days. If no date range is specified, the default search range is 7 days prior to the current date, inclusive.

A match is defined as the creation date falling within the search date range.
  - authorizations[].createDate

The result is a list of zero or more authorizations. If there are no matches, status 200, an empty authorizations[] array, and pageMeta.totalCount = 0 are returned.

### Initiating a search

These parameters can be set in the first request or will be defaulted:
- startDate
- endDate
- pageSize

They should **not** be used when retrieving page 2 and later.

`GET /cards/12345678/authorizations?startDate=2023-08-14&endDate=2023-09-06&pageSize=100`

### Retrieving a series of pages

The first response includes a **_searchKey_** representing the initiated search:

`"searchKey":"koFEcjwQYXn0ZKGc"`

The searchKey is used by the service for session management and is required in all subsequent requests. To simplify this process, the response also includes the **_pageMeta.links.next_** string which is the URI to retrieve the next page:

`"next":"/cards/12345678/authorizations?searchKey=koFEcjwQYXn0ZKGc&pageNumber=2"`

All subsequent requests require the _searchKey_ and _pageNumber_ parameters exactly as provided in the _next_ link.

To retrieve all pages, advance the pageNumber parameter in consecutive requests until the last page number indicated by **_pageMeta.pageCount_**.

- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/authorizations?searchKey=koFEcjwQYXn0ZKGc&pageNumber=2
- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/authorizations?searchKey=koFEcjwQYXn0ZKGc&pageNumber=3
- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/authorizations?searchKey=koFEcjwQYXn0ZKGc&pageNumber=...

The searchKey expires after 15 minutes and attempted use returns '400 Invalid Request'.

get.summary: List all transactions for this card.
get.description:
Return a list of all transactions for the card, including transaction and merchant details.

The search range begins on the card effectiveStart date through 1 year after the effectiveUntil date, inclusive. Up to 6 years of transaction history are retained.

The result is a list of zero or more transactions. If there are no matches, status 200 and an empty transactions[] array are returned.

### Initiating a search

To initiate a search, these parameters are required in the first request or are defaulted as specified:
- pageSize: default 1000
- pageNumber: default 1

`GET /cards/12345678/transactions?pageSize=1000`

### Retrieving a series of pages

The response includes the pageMeta.links.next string, which is the GET URI to retrieve the next page:

`"next":"/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=2"`

All subsequent requests require the *pageNumber* parameter, exactly as provided in the *next* link.

To retrieve all pages, simply advance the pageNumber parameter in consecutive requests until the last page number indicated by ***pageMeta.pageCount***.

- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=2
- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=3
- GET /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=...

post.summary: Return transactions for this card matching the search criteria.
post.description:
Returns a list of all transactions for the card matching the transaction date range specified in the request body. Up to 6 years of transaction history are retained.

The default date range is the maximum date range of:
- startDate = card effectiveStart date
- endDate   = card effectiveUntil date + 1 year

The start and end dates are inclusive.

 A match is defined as the transaction date falling within the date range.
  - transactions[].date

The result is a list of zero or more transactions. If there are no matches, status 200 and an empty transactions[] array are returned.

### Initiating a search

These parameters are required in the first request or are defaulted as specified below:
- pageSize: default 1000
- pageNumber: default 1

```
POST /cards/12345678/transactions?pageSize=1000
{
  "startDate": "2025-08-01",
  "endDate": "2025-08-31"
}
```

### Retrieving a series of pages

The response includes the pageMeta.links.next string, which is the GET URI to retrieve the next page:

`"next":"/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=2"`

```
POST /cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=2
{
  "startDate": "2025-08-01",
  "endDate": "2025-08-31"
}
```

All subsequent requests require the *pageNumber* parameter, exactly as provided in the *next* link. The request body must be repeated in each request.

To retrieve all pages, simply advance the pageNumber parameter in consecutive requests until the last page number indicated by ***pageMeta.pageCount***.

- POST /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=2
- POST /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=3
- POST /virtual-cards/v2/cards/12345678/transactions?pageNumber=...

Table_DeclinedAuthCodes.description:
This schema is provided for reference only. It describes the codes returned in:
- Real-Time Authorization webhook _eventDetails.decline.reason_
- AuthorizationSearchResponse _authorizations[].decline.reason_

The table below describes common declined authorization codes. The processing system assigns these codes to transactions that the merchant declines at the point of sale.

In the text of the account authorizations, you may encounter these terms
- *velocity* refers to the authorization limits set for cardholder accounts and managing accounts
- *corporate* refers to the managing account authorization limits
- *individual* refers to the cardholder account authorization limits

This table was last updated November 4, 2021.

|Code|Reason|Description|
|---|---|---|
|0001|Caution Account|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is flagged as a fraud/caution account.|
|0002|Closed Account|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is a closed account.|
|0003|Arrest|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is a confirmed fraud account with a credit rating set to fraud.|
|0004|Pick-Up - Fraud Code F1|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction has an F1 fraud status due to the plastic card being flagged as lost, stolen or never received by the cardholder. This decline reason may also display for an account with a F1 fraud status due to fraudulent activity on the account despite the cardholder possessing the card.|
|0005|Transferred Account|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction has been reported as lost or stolen, and the balance transferred to a new account, but the attempted transaction used the old account.|
|0006|Lost Card - Pending Transfer|The account the customer used for the transaction is a reported lost or stolen card with a balance that the customer has not yet transferred to a new card.|
|0007|Card Expired|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is an expired card.|
|0008|Charge-off Account|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is an account that has been charged-off.|
|0015|Account Coded V9|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is a closed account.|
|0016|Account Coded M9|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is a suspended account.|
|0031|Account Coded (Credit Rating)|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction has a negative credit rating.|
|0038|Obtain Positive ID|The account the customer used for this transaction has a fraud credit rating because of suspicious activity or potential fraud on the account.|
|0048|Not Enough Available Money|The attempted transaction would send the account over the account's available credit limit.|
|0084|Over Limit|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction is already over its allotted limit.|
|0091|Single Purchase Limit Exceeded|The attempted transaction exceeds the account's single purchase limit.|
|0092|Nmbr Monthly Transactions Exceeded|The attempted transaction would have exceeded the account's allowed number of monthly transactions.|
|0093|Nbr Daily Transaction Exceeded|The attempted transaction would have exceeded the account's allowed number of daily transactions.|
|0103|Invalid Card/Account|The card and/or account the customer used for the attempted transaction is not a valid card and/or account.|
|0111|Invalid PIN|The customer entered an invalid personal identification number. This authorization check applies to corporate cards used for travel purposes.|
|0112|Exceeds ATM Daily Limit|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction has exceeded the allowed daily dollar value of ATM withdrawals. This authorization check applies to corporate cards used for travel.|
|0113|Exceeded Number of ATM Per Day|The account the customer used for the attempted transaction has exceeded the allowed number of automated teller machine (ATM) transactions for that day. This authorization check applies to corporate cards used for travel.|
|0114|Exceeds PIN Limit|The cardholder entered their PIN incorrectly multiple times and the client or the bank needs to reset the PIN counter.|
|0117|Exceeds Down-Time Processing Limit|The processing system was down and the system could not process the attempted transaction.|
|0124|Invalid Card Verification Value/Check|The card verification value the customer gave for the attempted transaction did not match the card verification value on file for the account. This authorization check normally occurs for cardless accounts and for internet and telephone orders.|
|0125|Invalid Card Verification|The merchant is removing the card from the terminal too quickly and the merchant needs to retry the transaction, refer the transaction to merchant services, or swipe the card.|
|0134|CRV Status|The cardholder has not yet activated the account they used for the attempted transaction.|
|0145|ATC Incorrect|The card verification value (CVV) embedded in the chip is not verifying and the merchant needs to retry the transaction, refer the transaction to merchant services, or swipe the card.|
|0162|Invalid ICVV|The merchant is truncating the data they send and the merchant needs to retry the transaction, refer the transaction to merchant services, or swipe the card.|
|0333|Card Not Activated|The cardholder has not yet activated the account they used for the attempted transaction.|
|0800|Vendor Excluded|The merchant for the attempted transaction is excluded from the organization's preferred vendor list.|
|0803|MCCG Exclude|The transaction was with a merchant in a merchant category code group with a control set to exclude transactions.|
|0805|Exceeded Account Single Trans Limit|The transaction exceeds the account's single transaction limit.|
|0808|Exceeded MCCG STDL|The attempted transaction exceeded the single transaction limit for the merchant category code group associated to the account.|
|0813|Exceeded Account Velocity Amount|The attempted transaction exceeds a velocity limit set for the account.|
|0818|Exceeded Account MCCG Velocity Amount|The attempted transaction exceeds a velocity limit for the merchant category code group associated to the account.|
|0823|MCCG Included, No Match|The attempted transaction is with a merchant not in an authorized merchant category code group with a control set to approve only those included merchants.|
|0831|Invalid Plastic Used|The account the customer used for the transaction does not have a plastic card issued, but the authorization request indicates that someone swiped a card.|
|0832|No Driver or Vehicle in ISO MSG|The attempted transaction requires the submission of a Driver ID or Vehicle ID and neither was submitted by the merchant system.|
|0836|Invalid Fleet ID|The attempted transaction has an invalid fleet ID.|
|0837|Invalid Fleet Vehicle|The attempted transaction has an invalid fleet vehicle ID.|
|0838|Invalid Fleet Driver|The attempted transaction has an invalid fleet driver ID.|
|0851|ADS I Strategy|The authorization request hit an Authorization Decision Strategy I (ADS I) rule. ADS I includes pre-defined, high-risk fraud criteria.|
|0881|ARQC Invalid|The merchant ran the attempted transaction off-line and needs to run the transaction again on-line.|
|0882|Application Trans Counter Invalid|The merchant terminal is sending incomplete data and the merchant needs to retry the transaction, refer the transaction to merchant services, or swipe the card.|
|8997-9000|ADS II Strategy|The authorization went through an Authorization Decision Strategy II (ADS II) filter without hitting an ADS II rule. ADS II includes pre-defined, high-risk fraud criteria.|
|9001-9050|ADS II Strategy|The authorization request hit an ADS II rule. ADS II includes pre-defined, high-risk fraud criteria.|

Precise Pay ensures a single transaction will be authorized to the exact payment amount. _This is only available for the Single Use Account SUA program._

- true = enabled
- false = disabled

If unspecified, it will default to the client configuration or supplier record as applicable.

ControlNumber.description: User-assigned number usually referencing an invoice or purchase order number. This value should be unique unless the client is configured to allow duplicate control numbers. This value is required if the system is not configured to automatically generate a value. Alphanumeric and special characters are allowed.

Optional user-specified name:value pairs associated with the card.

The 'name' must match a name that has been previously configured. (It cannot be dynamically assigned.) It is case-sensative and may contain alphanumeric and special characters.

The 'value' is defined by the user and may contain alphanumeric and special characters, or an empty string "".

UserAttributes.description:
These are optional user-specified attributes that can be used to store any information.

This object cannot be empty - at least one value is required. Use an empty string to clear a value.

The customAttributes[] are also available.

Cardholder.description:
Customer name for virtual account number (VAN).

A name is required if the card will be push-provisioned to a digital wallet. If not provided, encrypting the card for push-provisioning will fail.

AuthStatusModify.description:
Indicates whether the virtual account number is available for purchase activity. A card in ACTIVE status will evaluate all other authorization rules to make an approval decision.  A Card in INACTIVE status will automatically reject all authorizations without evaluating any other controls.

By default a card is set to 'ACTIVE'

* ACTIVE - Authorization controls are enforced.
* INACTIVE - All authorizations will be declined.

PreAuthorization.description:
Specifies the pre-authorization amount for the card. Merchants can use pre-authorization to test the validity of a card.

If the amount is set to 0, then pre-authorization is not enabled. If it is greater than 0, then pre-authorization is set for the account. The amount cannot exceed the amount of the virtual card.

Minimum of 0 and maximum of 9999999.99

singlePurchaseLimit.description:
Amount allowed for each individual authorization request. The authorization request is considered for approval if it is less than or equal to the single authorization limit.

If *amount* is zero, the limit is disabled. Otherwise, the limit is enforced.

enforceAmountRanges.description:
Indicates whether VAN authorization amounts are limited to the ranges defined in _amountRanges[]_ for authorization requests.

When creating or updating a card:
- true = amountRanges[] are required and will be enforced.
- false = amountRanges[] are disabled and will not be enforced.

LimitAuthorizationCommon.description: There are a variety of controls including maximum amount for each purchase, velocity limits for controlling purchases within a time period, and amount ranges for controlling minimum and maximum purchase amounts.

count.description: Maximum number of transactions within this period.
Maximum number of transactions within this period.

start.description: Start date of the first period YYYY-MM-DD

end.description: End date defines the number of days in the custom period, where N days = end - start + 1 (inclusive)

LimitCustom.description:
Define a custom period. The length of the period is the number of days (N days) between the start and end dates, inclusive. The first period begins on the start date and repeats every N days.

Either amount or count is required or both. If *amount* or *count* is zero, that limit is disabled. If both *amount* and *count* are zero, the *start* and *end* dates are also disabled.

amountRanges.description:
If _enforceAmountRanges_ = true, this array is required and ranges will be enforced.
If _enforceAmountRanges_ = false, this array should not be present and ranges are not enforced. When enforced, authorization amounts must be within an amount range or will be declined. An amount range defines the minimum and maximum purchase limit allowed, inclusive. The minimum must be less than or equal to the maximum. Ranges cannot overlap. Up to 10 ranges can be defined. Each range is assigned a sequenceNumber (index) by the system, which is returned in the create response and read response.

LimitAmountNumber.description:
Minimum amount is 0 and maximum amount is 9999999.99.
Must be 0 to clear the limit.

LimitDailyEffectiveTimes.description:
List of daily effective times when authorizations are allowed. The day and times are relative to the U.S. Eastern timezone (EST or EDT). Times are specified in 24-hour HH:MM format in the U.S. Eastern timezone.

Only 1 time range is allowed per day.

To reset a particular day, set start to "00:00" and end to "23:59".

By default, authorizations are allowed on any day at any time.

MCCRangesCreate.description:
Merchant Category Codes are four-digit numbers representing the type of merchant where a purchase is made. For example, "5251" represents hardware stores. See the Table_MerchantCategoryCodes[] for a list of MCCs.

Purchases are only allowed if the associated MCC is within an MCC range, inclusive.

An MCC range is defined by the lowest MCC allowed to the highest MCC allowed, inclusive. The lowest MCC must be less than or equal to the highest MCC. Up to 30 ranges can be defined. Ranges cannot overlap. The highest code cannot be "0000". Leading zeros are required.

Each range will be assigned a sequenceNumber (index) by the system, which is returned in the create response and read response.

If no ranges are defined, none are enforced.

CreateSupplierEnrolled.description:
This request is used when remitType=SupplierEnrolled.

Given the supplier ID, the supplier details are obtained from the Client-Supplier-Information (CSI) record. Any supplier details provided in the request override values from the record.

***These fields are conditionally required if they are not pre-defined in the CSI record***
- Payment Account ID
- Supplier name
- Supplier email or faxNumber

If successful, a remittance is sent as indicated by the supplier.sendMethod parameter. If EMAIL (default), the email address must be provided or available in the CSI record. If FAX, a US faxNumber must be provided or available in the CSI record.

These fields are only applicable if the payment account is part of virtual account number (VAN) program:
- userAttributes{}
- cardholderName
- authStatus
- preAuthorizationAmount
- authorizationControls{}
- dailyEffectiveTimes[]
- merchantCategoryCodeRanges[]

remitType.description: Indicates the system will remit to the supplier using the details from the predefined supplier record

ID_Supplier.description: Unique supplier ID of a CSI record. Alphanumeric and special characters permitted.

sendMethod.description:
Method to send remittance to supplier. EMAIL is the default. If EMAIL, the email address must be available.

If FAX, the faxNumber must be an available *US phone number*.

email.description:
Up to 3 email addresses separated by a semi-colon ';'. These recipients receive a link to the remit. See permitted characters noted above.

Requires EMAIL sendMethod.

ccEmail.description:
One or more CC email addresses separated by a semi-colon ';'. These recipients DO NOT receive a link to the remit. See permitted characters noted above.

Requires EMAIL sendMethod.

faxNumber.description:
Supplier's fax number without punctuation.

Requires FAX sendMethod and must be an available *US phone number*.

credentials.description: Credentials the supplier must use to access the remittance. Historically, this is referred to as the 'Zip Code', which served as the password.

note.description: This is an optional note that appears as "Payment notes" in the email to the supplier. Alphanumeric and special characters permitted.

Supplier.description:
Supplier details related to the remittance.

The **email** and **ccEmail** values are alphanumeric including this subset of special characters:

**! # $ % ' * + - / = ? ^ & ; _ ` { | } ~**

SupplierName.description: Supplier Name. Alphanumeric and special characters permitted.

If successful, a remittance is sent as indicated by the supplier.sendMethod parameter. If EMAIL (default), the email address must be provided. If FAX, a US faxNumber must be provided.

amountRanges.description:
If _enforceAmountRanges_ = true, this array is required and ranges will be enforced.
If _enforceAmountRanges_ = false, this array should not be present and ranges are not enforced. When enforced, authorization amounts must be within an amount range or will be declined. An amount range defines the minimum and maximum purchase limit allowed, inclusive. The minimum must be less than or equal to the maximum. Ranges cannot overlap. Up to 10 ranges can be defined. Each range is assigned a sequenceNumber (index) by the system, which is returned in the create response and read response. - To modify a range, specify the sequenceNumber of the range to update. _Changing the minimum or maximum limit of an existing range will reset the tracked monetary authorization total for that range._ - To add a range, specify the next sequenceNumber for appending to the array. - To clear a range, set the minimum and maximum to zero for that sequenceNumber.

MCCRanges.description:
Merchant Category Codes are four-digit numbers representing the type of merchant where a purchase is made. For example, "5251" represents hardware stores. See the Table_MerchantCategoryCodes[] for a list of MCCs.

Purchases are only allowed if the associated MCC is within an MCC range, inclusive.

An MCC range is defined by the lowest MCC allowed to the highest MCC allowed, inclusive. The lowest MCC must be less than or equal to the highest MCC. Up to 30 ranges can be defined. Ranges cannot overlap. The highest code cannot be "0000". Leading zeros are required.

Each range will be assigned a sequenceNumber (index) by the system, which is returned in the create response and read response.
- To modify a range, specify the sequenceNumber of the range to update.

LimitAuthorizationCommon_velocity.description:
Velocity limits define maximum totals (amount) and maximum occurances (count) within the given time period.
If *amount* or *count* is zero, that limit is disabled. Otherwise, the limit is enforced.

day.description: Day of the week allowed for authorization.

start.description: HH:MM begin time of day for allowed authorizations in Eastern Time (EST or EDT).

end.description: HH:MM end time of day for allowed authorizations in Eastern Time (EST or EDT).

authorizationAmountUsed.description:
Indicates whether an authorization or transaction has been successfully processed for an amount that falls within this range.
- true = An authorization occurred within this range.
- false = No authorizations have occurred within this range.

sequenceNumber.description: The sequenceNumber is assigned by the system when the card is created and is returned when creating or reading a card.

lowest.description: Must be "0000" to clear a range.

highest.description: Must be "0000" to clear a range.

code.description:
3 part error code AAA.1042.CCCC
* AAA = 3-Digit HTTP status code
* 1042 = 4-Digit code assigned to this service
* CCCC = 4-Digit reason code from the service

details.description: Optional array indicating 1 or more fields in error

email.description: Up to 3 email addresses separated by a semi-colon ';'. These recipients receive a link to the remit. See permitted characters noted above.

ccEmail.description: One or more CC email addresses separated by a semi-colon ';'. These recipients DO NOT receive a link to the remit. See permitted characters noted above.

note.description: This is an optional note that appears as "Payment notes" in the email to the supplier. Alphanumeric and special characters permitted.

VirtualCard_Update_supplier.description:
Supplier attributes can be modified if the remitType when created was
- SupplierEnrolled
- SupplierNotEnrolled
